statement.conclusion: There exists a 1/(n+1)-centerpoint. For nonzero v, absolute continuity also gives mu(H_c(v))>=1/(n+1).
statement.objects_and_definitions: For v nonzero in T_x M, H_x(v)={Exp_x(w):<w,v>_x<0}. A beta-centerpoint c satisfies mu(H_c(v))<=1-beta for every v (the zero vector gives an empty halfspace).
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every mu as stated there exists such a c; if support is contained in S, a centerpoint can be chosen in S.
